literal: Anger, which is called the killer of those who associate with it, will burn the protective raft called kinship.
translation: Anger, the fire that destroys those who harbor it, will burn down the protective raft of one's family and friends.
modern: தன்னைச் சேர்ந்தவர்களையே அழிக்கும் நெருப்பாகிய சினம், ஒருவருக்குப் பாதுகாப்பாக இருக்கும் சுற்றம் என்னும் தெப்பத்தையும் எரித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful metaphor to warn against anger. It describes anger as 'சேர்ந்தாரைக் கொல்லி'—a fire that destroys the very person who harbors it. Furthermore, this destructive fire does not stop there; it spreads to burn down 'இனம் என்னும் ஏமப்புணை', which is the protective raft of one's relatives and friends. Just as a raft saves a person from drowning in a stormy sea, one's kin protect them from life's hardships, but anger completely destroys this vital support system.
